_note: Works of the twentieth-century reception, one record each. tier: A full text (public domain), B freely available elsewhere and linked, C own copy (anchor table only), D reference only. status says how far the work is in the apparatus. Hand-maintained; checked 21 November 2026.

works.author: W. H. Longridge, SSJE
works.title: The Spiritual Exercises of Saint Ignatius of Loyola. Translated from the Spanish with a Commentary and a Translation of the Directorium in Exercitia
works.imprint: London: Robert Scott, 1919
works.note: An Anglican religious of the Society of St John the Evangelist, not a Jesuit: four years after Rickaby, a full commentary from outside the Society. His commentary is cut at his own headings into blocks and mapped editorially onto the paragraph grid, which his book predates; taken over from Ignatiana.

works.author: Joseph Rickaby, SJ
works.title: The Spiritual Exercises of St. Ignatius Loyola: Spanish and English, with a Continuous Commentary
works.status: in the apparatus: his notes, from the second edition of 1923
works.imprint: First edition 1915; second edition London: Burns Oates & Washbourne, 1923, which is the text used here. Page numbers are those of 1923
works.rights: US public domain (both editions published before 1931).

sources.label: Google Books F7kHAQAAIAAJ (2nd ed. 1923, Stanford copy)

works.note: Rickaby prints the Spanish autograph and his translation in two columns, with notes across the page after each piece. He rearranges the book for use in a retreat: the Presupposition stands before the Annotations, the Examens follow the Additions, each set of rules for discernment follows its Week, the Mysteries of the Life of Christ are worked into the days of the Second Week, the rules on alms and scruples follow the Election. His notes are placed on the paragraphs whose text they follow, found by matching his Spanish column against the autograph (tools/rickaby_extract.py); a set of notes that follows text from two places of his order is shown at both. The text is Google's machine reading, not corrected by hand; the translation is not yet shown.

works.author: Alfred Feder, SJ (1872–1927)
works.title: Ignatius von Loyola, Geistliche Übungen. Nach dem spanischen Urtext übertragen, eingeleitet und mit Anmerkungen versehen
works.status: in the apparatus: German layer of the centre text, paragraph-exact on [1]–[370]
works.imprint: 2nd, improved and enlarged edition (3rd–5th thousand). Regensburg: Verlagsanstalt vorm. G. J. Manz, 1922
works.rights: US public domain (published 1922); public domain in Germany as well, the translator having died in 1927.

sources.label: Internet Archive MN5044ucmf_5 (University of Chicago microfilm)

works.note: Published for the fourth centenary of the book (1522/23); the preface says a new edition was needed within barely six months. The German layer of the centre column (language button 'de'). The text is the Internet Archive's ABBYY reading of the microfilm, rebuilt into paragraphs without running heads and footnotes (tools/feder_extract.py), corrected against a German dictionary with every change logged and some 250 forms read in context (tools/feder_fix.py), and put on the 1928 grid by an editorial anchor table compiled by reading Feder beside the Spanish (tools/feder_anchors.json, checked by tools/feder_check.py). Residual reading errors remain; Feder's italics, which mark words he supplied, are not reproduced; his footnotes and endnotes are left out. Some mystery headings were lost in the scan.

works.author: Erich Przywara, SJ
works.title: Deus semper maior. Theologie der Exerzitien
works.status: all three volumes anchored page by page from their tables of contents (148 anchors)
works.imprint: 3 vols. Freiburg im Breisgau: Herder, 1938–1940; 2nd ed. Wien/München: Herold, 1964
works.rights: Protected: in Germany until the end of 2042 (author d. 1972), in the US until 2033–2035.
works.note: The first tier-C work with a page anchor table (data/src/przywara_anchors.json): where each part of the Exercises is treated, by volume and page, read from the table of contents of the borrowed Internet Archive scan and checked at three places in the text (scan leaf = printed page + 22 in volume I). The table carries no text of Przywara's; the descriptions are mine. Like Rickaby, Przywara rearranges: he treats the rules for discernment of the First Week inside the First Week (vol. I, pp. 245-256), and he places the Additions and the forms of prayer before the five exercises; in volume II the Second Week runs over fourteen days of mysteries, the second rules for discernment stand on the sixth day (the day of the Two Standards and the Three Classes), and the three kinds of humility and the election come after the seventh day; in volume III the rules on eating, alms and scruples stand on the first day of the Third Week and the rules for thinking with the Church at the end of the Fourth Week, before the Contemplation to Attain Love. Volume III ends with Przywara's own index of the numbers of the Exercises (pp. 438-440), in the 1928 numbering; several anchors were checked against it. The Internet Archive scan without a volume field (deussempermaiort0000eric) is volume II, as its title page shows.
